summary: The bill directs the EPA to revise its phosphogypsum regulations within two years to require any new use approvals to be issued only on a case-by-case basis after submission of individual exposure-risk data, exposure-minimization plans, and quarterly surface/groundwater monitoring, while capping lifetime cancer risk at 9.1 in 100,000.

scores.thoughts: The bill directs the EPA to revise regulations on phosphogypsum distribution and use, requiring case-by-case approvals, risk assessments, exposure minimization plans, and monitoring programs. No provisions alter federal spending levels, authorize new appropriations, or affect budgets. It is purely regulatory.
The bill contains no tax provisions, rate changes, credits, or revenue measures of any kind.
While the bill references cancer risks from radiation exposure, it does not address healthcare delivery, insurance, coverage, or medical systems. It is an environmental regulation bill.
No provisions relate to firearms, regulations, or rights.
No provisions relate to immigration, borders, or pathways.
No provisions relate to reproductive rights or abortion access.
No provisions relate to military or defense spending.

The bill strengthens EPA oversight of phosphogypsum (a radioactive byproduct) by mandating stricter risk thresholds, case-by-case approvals, exposure minimization for workers and residents, leachate and ecotoxicity monitoring, and public disclosure. It explicitly reinforces the existing prohibition on road use due to environmental and health risks from radionuclides and groundwater contamination. This directly expands environmental protections and regulatory stringency.
No provisions relate to welfare programs, food assistance, or social safety net programs.
No provisions relate to schools, education funding, or school choice.
No provisions relate to drug enforcement or decriminalization.
No provisions relate to sentencing, policing, or criminal justice reform.
No provisions relate to trade, tariffs, or globalization.
No provisions relate to deficits, debt reduction, or fiscal policy.
No provisions relate to LGBTQ+ legal protections.
No provisions relate to foreign aid.
No provisions relate to voting access or election integrity.
No provisions relate to technology regulation or data privacy.
The bill mentions exposure risks to construction and utility workers but does not address union rights, worker protections in labor law, or employer flexibility.
No provisions relate to religious exemptions or civil rights priorities.
